advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the both-sides-keyed single-issuelink case is impossible from Jira (or add a fallback in map_remote_links to register both keys) so the 'byte-identical' dedup claim holds.
evidence: backend.py:230: `other_key, relation = resolve_inbound_link(link)` then appends a single `(relation, other_key, type_name)` per link
link_direction.py:43-46: resolve_inbound_link returns outwardIssue first, else inwardIssue — never both
Deleted `_existing_jira_links` looped BOTH sides: `for side_key in ("inwardIssue", "outwardIssue"): ... existing.add((type_name, side_key_val))`
ABSENCE: real Jira issuelinks carry exactly ONE of inward/outward per entry, so this divergence is only reachable on malformed/synthetic input; no test exercises a both-sides-keyed single link
advisory.finding: The commit message claims the new direction-agnostic ADD dedup is 'byte-identical to today's', but for a malformed single Jira issuelink carrying BOTH inwardIssue.key and outwardIssue.key the two implementations diverge: old `_existing_jira_links` registered both keys, whereas new `map_remote_links` (via `resolve_inbound_link`, outward-first) registers only one — so a local dep to the un-registered side would no longer be deduped and would emit an ADD.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct map_remote_links test asserting an unmapped vendor link type yields a `(None, remote_key, vendor_type)` entry (surfaced, not dropped).
evidence: Impl contract: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py:217 — 'An unmapped vendor link type still yields an entry, with relation=None, so core never removes a link it cannot canonicalize.'
test_canonical_link_diff.py:92-93 asserts only `("blocks", "DIG-9", "Blocks") in canonical` — membership of a MAPPED entry; no assertion for an unmapped type yielding `(None, key, type)`.

test_canonical_link_diff_heldout.py:91-101 (`test_unknown_remote_link_type_ignored_for_matching`) asserts the ADD still emits; for a 'Mentions' remote link vs a 'blocks' dep the ADD dedup keys on ('Blocks', 'DIG-9') which never matches ('Mentions','DIG-9'), so the assertion holds identically whether map_remote_links surfaces `(None,'DIG-9','Mentions')` or drops it — regression-blind to the surfacing contract.
advisory.finding: The core safety contract of the new map_remote_links — that an UNMAPPED vendor link type is SURFACED as a (relation=None, remote_key, vendor_type) entry rather than dropped (so core 'never removes a link it cannot canonicalize') — is not asserted by any test. The one direct test only checks a mapped Blocks link is in the result; the heldout 'unknown remote type' test observes ADD behavior that is byte-identical whether the entry is surfaced-with-None or dropped entirely, so it cannot detect a regression in the surfacing behavior.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert backend.map_remote_links({"issuelinks": [_link("Mentions", outward="DIG-9")]}) == [(None, "DIG-9", "Mentions")]` (and a mixed case with a mapped + unmapped link) to pin the surfacing contract.

No test in test_link_removal_sync.py injects an unmapped vendor type (e.g. 'Mentions') into a managed link to reach the line-157 branch.
advisory.finding: The `if relation is None: continue` guard in _diff_link_removals (the code that prevents an unmapped-type remote link from being removed) is not exercised by any REMOVE-pass test. All REMOVE tests inject mapped 'Blocks' links; none places an unmapped-type link (relation=None) into managed_refs to verify it is left for inbound ADOPT via the None-skip specifically (as distinct from the managed-ref gate).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test injecting an unmapped-type issuelink (e.g. {"type":{"name":"Mentions"},"outwardIssue":{"key":"PROJ-2"}}) with managed_refs=[["blocks","local-2"]] and deps=[], asserting no REMOVE mutation is emitted.
